title: Psalms Chapter 101 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Psalms chapter 101 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Psalms Chapter 101 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Psalms Chapter 101.

questions.question: According to Psalms 101:1, what will David sing of?
questions.explanation: David states that he will sing of mercy and judgment unto the LORD in Psalms 101:1.

questions.question: In Psalms 101:2, how does David say he will behave himself?
questions.explanation: David declares he will behave himself wisely in a perfect way as written in Psalms 101:2.

questions.question: What does David say he will do within his house according to Psalms 101:2?
questions.explanation: David says he will walk within his house with a perfect heart in Psalms 101:2.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 101:3 states that David will set wicked things before his eyes.
questions.explanation: David clearly states in Psalms 101:3 that he will set no wicked thing before his eyes.

questions.question: According to Psalms 101:3, what will David do with the work of those who turn aside?
questions.explanation: David says he hates the work of them that turn aside in Psalms 101:3.

questions.question: Which of the following does David say shall not cleave to him in Psalms 101:3?
options: The work of those who turn aside
questions.correctAnswer: The work of those who turn aside
questions.explanation: In Psalms 101:3, David states that the work of those who turn aside shall not cleave to him.

questions.question: True or False: In Psalms 101:1, David sings unto the LORD.
questions.explanation: David declares he will sing unto the LORD in Psalms 101:1.

questions.question: What question does David ask in Psalms 101:2?
options: When wilt thou come unto me?
questions.correctAnswer: When wilt thou come unto me?
questions.explanation: David asks 'O when wilt thou come unto me?' in Psalms 101:2.

questions.question: According to Psalms 101:1, who is the one David will sing unto?
questions.explanation: David clearly says he will sing unto the LORD in Psalms 101:1.

questions.question: Which comes first according to Psalms 101:1-3?
options: David will set no wicked thing before his eyes
David will sing of mercy and judgment
David will walk within his house with a perfect heart
questions.correctAnswer: David will sing of mercy and judgment
questions.explanation: Psalms 101:1 shows David first declares he will sing of mercy and judgment before mentioning other actions in verses 2 and 3.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 101:2 says David will walk within his house with a perfect heart.
questions.explanation: David states in Psalms 101:2 that he will walk within his house with a perfect heart.

questions.question: What is David’s attitude toward wicked things according to Psalms 101:3?
options: He sets no wicked thing before his eyes
questions.correctAnswer: He sets no wicked thing before his eyes
questions.explanation: David explicitly says in Psalms 101:3 that he will set no wicked thing before his eyes.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT mentioned in Psalms 101:1-3?
options: Walking within the house with a perfect heart
Setting wicked things before the eyes
questions.explanation: Building a temple is not mentioned in Psalms 101:1-3, while the other options are clearly stated.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 101:3 says David will hate the work of those that turn aside.
questions.explanation: David explicitly states in Psalms 101:3 that he hates the work of those who turn aside.

questions.question: According to Psalms 101:2, David’s behavior is described as which of the following?
questions.explanation: David says he will behave himself wisely in a perfect way in Psalms 101:2.

medium.title: Psalms Chapter 101 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Psalms Chapter 101 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Psalms 101:4, what kind of heart will depart from the psalmist?
questions.explanation: Psalms 101:4 explicitly states 'A froward heart shall depart from me,' indicating the psalmist desires to remove a crooked or perverse heart.

questions.question: What action does Psalms 101:5 say will be taken toward one who slanders a neighbor privily?
questions.explanation: Psalms 101:5 states 'Whoso privily slandereth his neighbour, him will I cut off,' showing the psalmist's refusal to tolerate secret slander.

questions.question: How does Psalms 101:6 describe those on whom the psalmist's eyes will be?
questions.explanation: Psalms 101:6 says, 'Mine eyes shall be upon the faithful of the land,' indicating the psalmist will focus on those who are loyal and upright.

questions.question: What result does Psalms 101:6 promise for those who walk in a perfect way?
options: They shall be honored by the people
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'he that walketh in a perfect way, he shall serve me,' showing a relationship of faithful service as a result of righteous living.

questions.question: According to Psalms 101:4-5, what kind of people will the psalmist refuse to associate with?
options: Wicked persons and those with proud hearts
questions.correctAnswer: Wicked persons and those with proud hearts
questions.explanation: Verse 4 says the psalmist will not know a wicked person, and verse 5 states he will not suffer those with a proud heart, showing a clear rejection of these attitudes.

questions.question: How does Psalms 101:5 describe the attitude of one with a 'high look' and what will the psalmist do about it?
options: Such a person will be honored
Such a person will not be suffered
Such a person will be taught kindness
Such a person will be ignored
questions.correctAnswer: Such a person will not be suffered
questions.explanation: The verse says, 'him that hath an high look and a proud heart will not I suffer,' showing the psalmist’s disapproval of arrogance.

questions.question: What does Psalms 101:4 teach about the relationship between the psalmist and wicked persons?
questions.explanation: The verse says, 'I will not know a wicked person,' meaning the psalmist will avoid close association with the wicked, showing a principle of separation.

questions.question: What does Psalms 101:6 imply about the importance of faithfulness in the community?
options: Faithful people should be watched and dwelled with
questions.correctAnswer: Faithful people should be watched and dwelled with
questions.explanation: The psalmist declares, 'Mine eyes shall be upon the faithful of the land, that they may dwell with me,' showing faithfulness is highly valued in community life.

questions.question: What does Psalms 101:5 teach about handling those who secretly slander others?
questions.explanation: The verse says, 'Whoso privily slandereth his neighbour, him will I cut off,' teaching that secret slander is severely condemned and must be dealt with decisively.

questions.question: According to Psalms 101:4-6, what is the connection between rejecting a froward heart and serving the psalmist?
options: Rejecting sin leads to walking perfectly and serving faithfully
Rejecting a froward heart causes isolation
Serving the psalmist requires ignoring wickedness
Walking in a perfect way causes pride
questions.correctAnswer: Rejecting sin leads to walking perfectly and serving faithfully
questions.explanation: Verse 4 states the psalmist will reject a froward heart; verse 6 connects walking in a perfect way to serving him, showing a progression from rejecting sin to faithful service.

questions.question: How does Psalms 101:6 teach us about integrity in leadership or fellowship?
options: Leaders should serve only the proud
Leaders should focus on the faithful and perfect walkers
questions.correctAnswer: Leaders should focus on the faithful and perfect walkers
questions.explanation: The verse says the psalmist’s eyes are on the faithful and that those who walk perfectly shall serve him, emphasizing integrity as a leadership criterion.

questions.question: If a believer follows the instruction in Psalms 101:4 to reject a froward heart, what does Psalms 101:6 promise regarding fellowship?
options: They will be isolated from others
They will dwell with the faithful and serve the psalmist
They will be subject to slander
questions.correctAnswer: They will dwell with the faithful and serve the psalmist
questions.explanation: Verse 4 emphasizes rejecting a corrupt heart, while verse 6 promises that those faithful and walking perfectly will dwell and serve, showing the blessing of godly fellowship.

questions.question: What does Psalms 101:5 suggest about humility and pride in community relationships?
options: Pride is not suffered, indicating a rejection of arrogance
questions.correctAnswer: Pride is not suffered, indicating a rejection of arrogance
questions.explanation: The verse says, 'him that hath an high look and a proud heart will not I suffer,' teaching that prideful attitudes harm community and must be rejected.

questions.question: What lesson does Psalms 101:6 give about the reward for those who live righteously?
questions.explanation: The verse states that those walking in a perfect way will serve him, indicating a close, honored relationship as a reward for righteousness.

questions.question: According to Psalms 101:4 and 5, how should a believer respond to wickedness and slander in their community?
questions.explanation: The psalmist declares he will not know a wicked person (verse 4) and will cut off those who slander (verse 5), teaching active rejection of wickedness rather than tolerance.

hard.title: Psalms Chapter 101 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Psalms Chapter 101.

questions.question: According to Psalms 101:7, who shall not dwell within the Psalmist's house?
options: He that walketh in a perfect way
questions.explanation: Psalms 101:7 explicitly states, 'He that worketh deceit shall not dwell within my house.'

questions.question: What action does the Psalmist declare he will do early according to Psalms 101:8?
options: Destroy all the wicked of the land
Walk within his house with a perfect heart
Set no wicked thing before his eyes
questions.correctAnswer: Destroy all the wicked of the land
questions.explanation: Psalms 101:8 states, 'I will early destroy all the wicked of the land; that I may cut off all wicked doers from the city of the LORD.'

questions.question: Which Old Testament book contains a similar injunction against deceit and lies as Psalms 101:7?
questions.explanation: Proverbs frequently condemns deceit and lying (e.g., Proverbs 6:16-19), paralleling Psalms 101:7's rejection of deceitful and lying persons.

questions.question: What is the Hebrew meaning of the word translated as 'deceit' in Psalms 101:7?
questions.explanation: The Hebrew root for 'deceit' (מִרְמָה, mirmah) means to twist or distort, indicating moral corruption, which aligns with Psalms 101:7's condemnation.

questions.question: In Psalms 101:8, the Psalmist aims to cut off wicked doers from which specific location?
questions.explanation: Psalms 101:8 clearly states the goal to 'cut off all wicked doers from the city of the LORD,' referencing Jerusalem or the holy city.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of removing wickedness and deceit similar to Psalms 101:7-8?
questions.explanation: Ephesians 5:11 instructs believers to 'have no fellowship with the unfruitful works of darkness, but rather reprove them,' echoing Psalms 101's rejection of deceit and wickedness.

questions.question: What literary device is prominently featured in Psalms 101:7, contrasting deceitful persons with those who dwell in the Psalmist's house?
questions.explanation: Psalms 101:7 uses antithetical parallelism, contrasting 'he that worketh deceit shall not dwell' with the implied righteous who do dwell, emphasizing moral exclusion.

questions.question: According to Psalms 101:6, who does the Psalmist keep his eyes upon?
questions.explanation: Psalms 101:6 states, 'Mine eyes shall be upon the faithful of the land, that they may dwell with me,' indicating the Psalmist's focus on faithful followers.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 101:5 indicates that the Psalmist will tolerate a proud heart among his companions.
questions.explanation: Psalms 101:5 states, 'him that hath an high look and a proud heart will not I suffer,' showing the Psalmist does not tolerate pride.

questions.question: Which theme in Psalms 101 is foreshadowed by the Psalmist's commitment to walk within his house with a perfect heart (Psalms 101:2)?
options: The establishment of a righteous kingdom
questions.correctAnswer: The establishment of a righteous kingdom
questions.explanation: Walking with a perfect heart in one's house (Psalms 101:2) foreshadows the ideal of a righteous kingdom led by a just ruler, a theme fulfilled in Davidic kingship.

questions.question: Which Psalm other than Psalms 101 also emphasizes the removal of wickedness from God's presence?
questions.explanation: Psalm 1 contrasts the wicked who perish like chaff with the righteous who delight in the law, echoing Psalms 101's emphasis on removing wickedness.

questions.question: What does the term 'tarry' in Psalms 101:7 imply about the presence of liars in the Psalmist's sight?
options: They will not remain or stay
questions.correctAnswer: They will not remain or stay
questions.explanation: 'Tarry' means to remain or stay, so Psalms 101:7 means liars will not be allowed to remain in the Psalmist's presence.

questions.question: True or False: The Psalmist in Psalms 101 expresses a desire to know wicked persons and keep them close.
questions.explanation: Psalms 101:4 states, 'A froward heart shall depart from me: I will not know a wicked person,' indicating the Psalmist avoids wickedness.

questions.question: How does Psalms 101:5's condemnation of slander connect with the teachings of Jesus in the New Testament?
options: It parallels Jesus' teaching to love your neighbor as yourself
It contradicts Jesus' teachings on forgiveness
It has no connection to New Testament teachings
It supports the practice of public shaming
questions.correctAnswer: It parallels Jesus' teaching to love your neighbor as yourself
questions.explanation: Psalms 101:5 condemns secret slander, aligning with Jesus' command to love one's neighbor (Matthew 22:39), opposing harmful speech.

questions.question: Which ancient Near Eastern cultural value is reflected in the Psalmist’s commitment to exclude deceitful and wicked persons from his community in Psalms 101?
questions.explanation: In the ancient Near East, the king's household was expected to be morally and ritually pure; Psalms 101 reflects this cultural value by excluding deceit and wickedness.

theological.title: Psalms Chapter 101 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Psalms Chapter 101 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What divine attribute is emphasized in David's commitment to sing in Psalms 101:1?
questions.explanation: Psalms 101:1 states, 'I will sing of mercy and judgment,' highlighting God's attribute of mercy alongside judgment.

questions.question: According to Psalms 101:2, what does David vow to maintain within his house?
questions.explanation: Psalms 101:2 says, 'I will walk within my house with a perfect heart,' indicating David's vow for inner purity in his household.

questions.question: What is David's stance toward wickedness as expressed in Psalms 101:3?
options: He will set no wicked thing before his eyes
He tolerates some wickedness for mercy
questions.correctAnswer: He will set no wicked thing before his eyes
questions.explanation: In Psalms 101:3, David clearly states, 'I will set no wicked thing before mine eyes,' demonstrating his rejection of sin's influence.

questions.question: What type of heart does David declare will depart from him in Psalms 101:4?
questions.explanation: Psalms 101:4 states, 'A froward heart shall depart from me,' illustrating David's commitment to reject perversity.

questions.question: Which behavior does David declare he will cut off according to Psalms 101:5?
questions.explanation: Psalms 101:5 specifies, 'Whoso privily slandereth his neighbour, him will I cut off,' showing David's intolerance of secret slander.

questions.question: What kind of individuals does David say his eyes will be upon in Psalms 101:6?
questions.explanation: Psalms 101:6 states, 'Mine eyes shall be upon the faithful of the land,' indicating David's focus on righteousness.

questions.question: According to Psalms 101:7, who shall not dwell within David's house?
questions.explanation: Psalms 101:7 states, 'He that worketh deceit shall not dwell within my house,' emphasizing exclusion of deceitful persons.

questions.question: What is David's declared purpose in destroying the wicked early as in Psalms 101:8?
options: To cut off all wicked doers from the city of the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: To cut off all wicked doers from the city of the LORD
questions.explanation: Psalms 101:8 says, 'I will early destroy all the wicked of the land; that I may cut off all wicked doers from the city of the LORD,' showing his zeal for holiness in God's city.

questions.question: What combined teaching do Psalms 101:3 and Psalms 101:7 convey about sanctification?
options: Believers must reject wickedness and deceit from their presence
One may tolerate some sin for the sake of peace
Wickedness is only external and not heart-deep
Truth and wickedness can coexist in the believer's life
questions.correctAnswer: Believers must reject wickedness and deceit from their presence
questions.explanation: Psalms 101:3 rejects setting wicked things before the eyes, and 101:7 excludes deceitful workers from the house, together teaching active separation from sin.

questions.question: How do Psalms 101:5 and Psalms 101:6 together inform the doctrine of church discipline?
options: Slanderers are to be cut off while the faithful are to dwell with the godly
All are to be tolerated regardless of conduct
Discipline is unnecessary in the assembly
Pride and slander are virtues within the church
questions.correctAnswer: Slanderers are to be cut off while the faithful are to dwell with the godly
questions.explanation: Psalms 101:5 promises cutting off slanderers, while 101:6 promises fellowship with the faithful, teaching the balance of discipline and fellowship.

questions.question: What theological doctrine is emphasized by David's desire in Psalms 101:2 to walk 'in a perfect way'?
questions.explanation: Walking 'in a perfect way' (Psalms 101:2) indicates a pursuit of holiness and moral perfection, central to the doctrine of sanctification.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that Psalms 101 teaches harsh intolerance of sinners. What does Psalms 101:4-5 actually teach about the believer's relationship to sin?
options: Believers must actively separate from sin and those who practice it
Believers should accept all sinners without distinction
Only public sinners are to be rejected
questions.correctAnswer: Believers must actively separate from sin and those who practice it
questions.explanation: Verses 4-5 declare removal of a froward heart and cutting off slanderers, showing the necessity of holy separation, not mere harshness (Psalms 101:4-5).

questions.question: What attribute of God is revealed by David's commitment in Psalms 101:8 to destroy the wicked early?
questions.explanation: David's resolve to destroy the wicked early (Psalms 101:8) reflects God's justice and holiness that cannot tolerate sin in His city.

questions.question: What narrative arc of redemption does Psalms 101:1-2 contribute to within the broader Scripture?
options: The covenantal relationship between God and His king
The fall of man and its consequences
The exile of Israel in Babylon
The establishment of the temple worship only
questions.correctAnswer: The covenantal relationship between God and His king
questions.explanation: David's vow to sing of mercy and judgment and walk in perfection (Psalms 101:1-2) reflects the ideal king's covenantal fidelity to God in Scripture's redemption story.

questions.question: How does the teaching of Psalms 101:6-7 reflect on the doctrine of the visible church?
options: The church is to be composed of the faithful and exclude deceitful persons
The church accepts all without distinction
The church is primarily a social club
The church does not distinguish between truth and falsehood
questions.correctAnswer: The church is to be composed of the faithful and exclude deceitful persons
questions.explanation: Psalms 101:6-7 differentiates between the faithful who serve and dwell with the king and those who work deceit, teaching that the visible church must hold to truth.
